summary: The island looks and behaves far better than at session 20. The follow camera finds groups and faces, the mini games have clear start and end cards, levels, bests and rewards, and waving a friend into a parade works on the first try. But playing every mini game for a minute like a first-time player, Sprout got stuck against a bush, a lantern or the pond in all three while the HUD kept saying 'ahead': the berry race was lost 8-5 after 48 s of running in place. Every round also slid into night, because an in-game hour lasts a minute. Up close the creatures are still primitive blobs, midday light is flat, and switching on path tracing at night ran the GPU out of memory. Between s43 and s46 the progress shots barely changed.

lighting.why: Raster midday is even and flat (no haze, no warm sun, saturated dark-green shadows). The night raster is charming (glowing cottage window, fireflies; reviews/p46/after-trace.png). The dusk trace (dance take 9) is murky, and live path tracing at 22:55 failed with a GPU out-of-memory error.

world.why: The overview has variety (pond, cottage, pier, beach cove, cairn spiral, golden field), but the s43 and s46 progress shots are nearly identical, and at eye level the meadow is a lawn of identical tufts. A day lasts 24 min, so most play happens at dusk or night.

props.why: 24 generated assets in use. Tree crowns show black slits in traced stills, cairn stones are uniform brown potatoes, and the builder crate is still a cube though its asset finished at 19:58.

creatures.why: Their behaviour is rich: waves answered then follow (Wibbles :answer -> :follow on the second E), fishing, dancing, sleeping with z's. Their shapes are balls and sticks with the same googly eyes, with no expressions and a stiff walk.

fun.why: The cards, HUD and levels are good, and the waves and parade work. But a first player gets stuck against solids in all three games with no way out shown: berry 5 picked in 12 s, then 48 s in place; hide and seek 3/4 in 25 s, then 45 s in place; fireflies 4/8 with the last 35 s at the pond edge 'nearest 2 m ahead'.

camera.why: Better than s43: the follow camera holds and cuts, frames faces and groups (3 of 5 follow shots good), and orbit gives a fine island view. Still: Sprout behind cattails with a creature cut at the edge (now-1.png), a shot from under a crown (follow-4.png), and steep near-top-down mini game views at night.

ui.why: The start and end cards are clear and the key bar lights up. But the 'Messages to you' panel is cut mid-sentence again, the Jump in help card covers the lower third of the view, the free-camera hint bar never fades (even in the progress shots), and the side panel is a wall of small text.

style.why: Toy-like and mostly cohesive. Generated textured assets (mushrooms, rocks, cottage) sit next to smooth untextured primitive creatures and stones.

performance.why: Frame median 2.6 ms, p95 4.5 ms during and after four minutes of driven play with 31 plugins, at a steady 30 fps.

findings.title: Mini games: Sprout gets stuck on solids while the HUD says 'ahead'
findings.what: I played each game for about a minute like a first-time player: hold W, turn towards the target the HUD names. All three got stuck. Berry race: 5 berries in the first 12 s, then Sprout ran in place against a lantern and bush for 48 s with 'berry 3 m ahead', and the critters won 8-5. Hide and seek: 3 of 4 friends found in 25 s, then 45 s in place beside a big bush and its followers with 'a giggle 15 m ahead'. Firefly catch: 4/8, with the last 35 s at the pond edge with 'nearest 2 m ahead' (a fly over the water). Nothing tells the player they are blocked or which way round to go.
findings.where: plugins/berry_race.jl, hideseek.jl, firefly_catch.jl (HUD direction and targets); separation.jl (blocking)
findings.evidence: reviews/p46/play-berry-sheet.png, play-hide-jump-sheet.png, play-firefly-sheet.png, reviews/p46/play/log.txt (HUD text every 12 s), driver reviews/p46/play.jl
findings.suggestion: Make Sprout slide along solids instead of stopping (steer the walk direction around the footprint, as a controller does in cozy games). Point the HUD and the light beam along a walkable route (a waypoint round the bush), not the straight line. Never let a firefly drift over water or into a nook. A tiny 'bonk' puff and a sideways nudge when W pushes into something for 1 s.
findings.done_when: reviews/p46/play.jl (straight-line steering at the HUD target, no S) scores ≥ 6 berries, finds 4/4 and catches ≥ 6/8 flies, and no 10 s stretch in any game leaves Sprout within 0.5 m of where it was while W is held.

findings.title: Distinct creature silhouettes: ears, tails, legs, faces with expression
findings.what: Every creature is a ball or fluffy blob on sticks with the same googly eyes. From the side the snootle, Sprout and the fluffkin read as the same white ball. Faces never change with mood (cheering at the berry race end looks the same as idling), and the walk is a stick shuffle. This is what fills most follow and mini game frames.
findings.evidence: media/s45/lineup-after.png; reviews/p46/sheet-cams.png; reviews/p46/play/berry-9end.png (the critters cheer 'Ha! We won!' with unchanged faces)
findings.suggestion: One signature silhouette part per species (long ears, a fluffy tail, a snout, chunky feet). Eye states driven by mood and action: ^ ^ when cheering or dancing, closed when asleep, wide when startled, a small mouth that opens. A squash-and-stretch hop in the walk. Batch the part-count changes into one engine restart.
findings.done_when: A lineup (tools/lineup.jl) rendered as black silhouettes tells all five species apart, and a screenshot of a mini game end card shows the cheering critters with changed eye shapes.

findings.title: Raster lighting: warm sun, soft coloured shadows, haze, readable dusk
findings.what: Midday is evenly lit and flat. Shadows are dark saturated green with no cool sky fill, and far trees are as saturated as near ones (no depth). In the dusk trace (dance take 9) the creatures are brown silhouettes on a near-black meadow.
findings.where: RayMakie raster lighting (SunSkyLight bake), scenery.jl sync_sun!
findings.suggestion: A sun colour that warms after 15:00 and a cool fill tint in the shadows (in RayMakie, since the raster ignores AmbientLight), plus distance haze towards the horizon colour. For dusk films, exposure or a key light so the faces read.
findings.done_when: At the same hour, the shadow B/G ratio in eye-level.png rises ≥ 15%, trees 40 m away are ≥ 25% less saturated than near trees, and a dusk traced frame has the creatures' faces at ≥ 0.25 mean luminance.

findings.title: Path tracing at night runs out of GPU memory in the live dashboard
findings.what: At 22:55 in the sandbox I switched to orbit and turned 'Path tracing: on'. Both screenshots 45 s and 65 s later failed with 'Failed to resolve trace_renderobject … LavaError during pool_alloc: cannot allocate 356 MB, 2.77 GB already reserved'. The failing plot is an emissive meshscatter (Emission 4.0, instances at z 30-90 m: the stars or sky glow) growing Hikari's DiffuseAreaLight array. A player who presses the button at night gets no picture; the raster came back once it was switched off.
findings.where: plugins/stars.jl (or nightglow) under NG.path_traced; Hikari area light resize (Mantle memory.jl:577)
findings.evidence: this review's live_screenshot error after live_path_tracing(true) at daytime 0.955; reviews/p46/after-trace.png (raster OK after off)
findings.suggestion: Stars and sky motes should not be area lights at all in path tracing: draw them as one emissive sky texture or a non-light emissive material. Fix the resize leak in Hikari (patches/raymakie-emissive-meshscatter-leak.md) rather than skipping plots.
findings.done_when: Path tracing on at 23:00 and at 12:00, two on/off cycles each, gives four screenshots without an error, and GPU memory after the second cycle is within 10% of the first.

findings.title: Longer day: every mini game round slides into night
findings.what: An in-game hour lasts about a minute (12:10 to 13:06 during the camera shots; my four games ran from 17:50 to 21:46). Every round I played started at dusk and ended in the dark, the berry race and hide and seek were played mostly at night, and half of any 24-minute visit is dark.
findings.evidence: the clock in reviews/p46/play/*.png (17:50 firefly start, 20:02 berry end, 21:46 jump in)
findings.suggestion: day_length 3600-4800 s (an hour of play is a day), with a slower night. Check the plugins that schedule by hour (beds, nightshots, showers, lamplight) and the saved world.json.
findings.done_when: Over a 5-minute live run, the clock advances ≤ 30 in-game minutes and night (night_factor > 0.5) covers ≤ 35% of the day.

findings.title: Tree crowns: no black slits, more crown shapes, leaf colour variety
findings.what: The broadleaf crowns show black slit holes that read as little faces or bullet holes in every traced still and close raster shot, and almost every broadleaf has the same lime blob crown on a red-orange trunk. Big dark crowns also fill the top half of the chase views in all three mini games.
findings.where: the generated tree assets and their materials
findings.suggestion: Close or backface-fill the crown cavities, add 2-3 more crown silhouettes (tall oval, wide flat, blossom tree), vary the leaf hue ±10% per instance.
findings.done_when: A traced still of three big trees shows no cluster darker than 0.05 inside a crown, and the overview shows at least three distinct crown shapes.

findings.title: Release the dance film (readable dancers), then the next
findings.what: Goal 2 has a first release ('One more stone' v2, 13 s, clean daylight). The dance film is not out: take 9 at the default hour is too dark to read the dancers, the golden-hour take 8 lost the GPU device four times, and there is no blog post.
findings.suggestion: Bisect the device loss at golden hour (2 s at 720p, then without the glow plugins), or film the dance by day. Cut it to 20-40 s with a title card.
findings.done_when: A new world/releases folder holds a dance film whose contact sheet shows every dancer's face at ≥ 0.25 luminance, with NOTE.md and a say_to_human with the path.

findings.title: A shareable moment: creatures play a game together and Sprout joins
findings.what: In Jump in, two waves bring Wibbles along, and that works well. After that the player has little to do with a friend: Space showed no visible hop in my shot, and nothing invites the player to play WITH critters (pass, chase, build) in a way worth showing someone.
findings.suggestion: One group game the player joins on a key: keep-up with the ball in a circle of three critters who count the passes and cheer, or tag. Framed by a group view, with a streak on screen.
findings.done_when: A 20 s screenshot sequence shows a steered Sprout and ≥ 2 critters passing or chasing in one framed group view, with an on-screen count the player raised with a key.

engine.what: Hikari area lights for an emissive meshscatter grow on every push until the Vulkan pool is exhausted. Live path tracing at night fails within 45 s.
engine.evidence: Mantle memory.jl:577 pool_alloc via resize!(LavaArray{DiffuseAreaLight}) from RayMakie plots/meshscatter.jl:379 trace_renderobject; 2.77 GB reserved, 356 MB requested

engine.what: The golden-hour dance clip loses the Vulkan device (VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST) at 96 and 48 samples; the same clip at the default hour finishes.
The RayMakie raster ignores AmbientLight, and SunSkyLight has no sun colour: a warm sun and coloured shadow fill need changes in RayMakie/Hikari.
Host: reviewers cannot queue worker jobs (world/jobs is read-only for them), so a traced still has to come from live path tracing in the sandbox.
engine.evidence: submit_job(:trace) -> SystemError Read-only file system, jobs/…-trace.json.tmp

process: Since s43 the author has worked on the weakest category, the camera, and it shows: holds, cuts, faces and group framing. Goal 1 moved with levels, bests, the parade and the builder show, and Goal 2 got its first release. But the mini game tests steer a bot that knows where everything is and are tuned until they pass; a real first play for a full minute gets stuck in every game, and nobody noticed because no test plays longer than 20-35 s or checks for being stuck. Goal 3 moved least: the two high findings from s43 (creature silhouettes #236, raster lighting #237) are still largely open after three sessions, and the s43 and s46 progress shots are almost the same picture. Session 46 spent most of its time on the builder (charming, but about the author's own publishing) and on test flakes. Next: unstick the mini games, lengthen the day, then go at the things in every frame (creature shapes and faces, light, crowns), each with before/after shots from the same camera.
response: s49: findings are open todos (#236 creatures: joy faces done as a first part, #237 lighting, #175 path tracing at night, #184 dance film, #223 shared play); the first-play stuck and day-length ones were addressed in s47.
